w:r.w:t: Maseer Group Customer Onboarding and Training Plan
Phase 1 rollout of Employee, Leave, Attendance, Settings and Dashboard modules
Maseer Group / Maseer Tech (final customer name to be confirmed)
Provide a practical, budget-conscious plan that can be executed without over-engineering the first customer rollout.
This document is structured for decision-making first, followed by implementation detail.
Purpose, partnership context and rollout recommendation
Role-based training programme and session plan
UAT, cutover, support and acceptance criteria

This plan covers the first DijiPeople customer rollout for Maseer Group or Maseer Tech. The final legal/customer name is intentionally left as a confirmation item. The commercial relationship is understood as a partnership in which Sir Saud owns Maseer Group and Taimur Israr owns DijiPeople. DijiPeople currently operates in association with Maseer Group but is expected to become a separate product/business over time.

Run a controlled Phase 1 rather than exposing every available module. Start with employee records, leave, attendance, tenant settings and dashboards; stabilise real usage; then release recruitment and onboarding as Phase 2.
Maseer has a configured tenant with accurate employee and organisation data.
Employees can access their profile, submit leave and use the agreed attendance method.
Managers can review attendance and approve or reject leave requests.
HR administrators can maintain employees, leave policies, attendance settings, holidays and user access.
Leadership can view trusted Phase 1 dashboard metrics.
DijiPeople has documented support, issue triage and change-control processes for its first production customer.
Employee master records, organisation placement, reporting manager, status, contact and employment information.
Leave types, policies, entitlement/balances, request, approval, rejection, cancellation and dashboard reporting.
Work schedules, weekends/holidays, attendance capture, late/early handling, exceptions and attendance views.
Employees, managers, HR, IT for desktop deployment.
Tenant branding, organisation structure, locations, departments, teams, roles, permissions and operational settings required by Phase 1.
DijiPeople administrator and Maseer HR/IT administrators.
Headcount, leave, attendance and operational summary cards using approved Phase 1 data.
Leadership, HR and managers subject to role access.
Recruitment, candidate pipeline and job management.
Employee onboarding workflows, joining documents and induction tasks.
Payroll, compensation, loans, benefits and statutory processing.
Performance management, learning, contracts, projects and advanced analytics.
Any integration that is not required for Phase 1 attendance, identity or notifications.
Employee, leave, attendance, settings and dashboard flows must pass staging regression and tenant-isolation tests.
Approximately 100 users is within the proposed starter infrastructure; attendance peak testing is required.
Maseer must provide complete, validated employee, hierarchy, leave-balance and schedule data by 14 August 2026.
The Electron installer must be signed or the unsigned-installation risk formally accepted. Test on representative Windows devices.
Requires one accountable Maseer HR lead, timely decisions and no major scope expansion.
Subject to UAT, production-readiness and training gates.

The production platform must be ready before customer cutover. If deployment, credentials, database backups or desktop packaging are not production-safe, move the go-live date rather than accepting avoidable risk.
Configure the standard product first. Avoid customer-specific code unless a confirmed business requirement cannot be met through tenant settings or reusable rules.
Use a train-the-trainer model: DijiPeople trains Maseer HR/admin champions, who then help reinforce employee adoption.
Use real Maseer processes and approved data in UAT, not generic demonstrations.
Maintain one controlled issue list with severity, owner, target date and release decision.
Freeze Phase 1 scope after the kickoff. New ideas go into the Phase 2 backlog unless they block legal, security or operational use.
Confirms business priority, resolves organisational blockers and approves go-live.
DijiPeople product owner and implementation lead
Owns product readiness, solution decisions, configuration, training, deployment coordination and final release recommendation.
Supplies data and policies, coordinates users, validates configuration, manages UAT and confirms acceptance.
Attend detailed training, verify employee/leave/attendance setup and provide first-line process support.
Supports user accounts, Windows desktop deployment, network access and local device troubleshooting.
Validate approval routing, attendance visibility and manager dashboards.
Test self-service, attendance and leave journeys before broad go-live.
Taimur, Maseer HR lead, IT as needed
Review progress, decisions, risks and blockers.
Classify issues, confirm fixes and protect go-live scope.
Sponsor or delegate, HR lead, Taimur
Review adoption, incidents and business continuity.
Accept Phase 1 and agree Phase 2 priorities.
Maseer should provide the first complete data pack by Friday, 14 August 2026. Late or incomplete data is the most likely cause of a delayed go-live.
Legal entity, business units, departments, teams, locations, designations and employee levels.
Names are unique; inactive structures are identified.
Employee code, name, work email, mobile, hire date, status, location, department/team, designation, level, manager and employment type.
Unique employee code/email; every active employee has a valid manager or approved exception.
Users requiring login, HR admins, managers, approvers and leadership dashboard viewers.
Leave types, entitlement, accrual, carry-forward, probation rules, attachments, approval route and balance as of cutover.
Balance total reconciles to existing HR record.
Workweek, weekends, holidays, shifts, grace periods, late/early rules, overtime treatment and permitted check-in modes.
Rules signed off and pilot devices identified.
Customer display name, logo, support contact and employee announcement approver.
Final customer name confirmed before production invitations.
Approved KPI definitions and visibility by role.
Counts reconcile to imported source data.
1. DijiPeople issues controlled Excel/CSV templates with required fields, examples and allowed values.
2. Maseer completes the files and performs an internal first review before submission.
3. DijiPeople validates duplicates, missing relationships, invalid dates, unsupported values and leave-balance totals.
4. A first import is performed in staging and a reconciliation report is returned.
5. Maseer corrects the source file rather than making uncontrolled staging edits where possible.
6. The approved final file is frozen for production cutover and retained as migration evidence.
7. Post-import checks confirm employee count, active/inactive count, manager relationships, balances, shifts and role access.
Use “Maseer Group” as the working name until confirmed.
Desktop agent for office devices plus authorised administrative correction; avoid multiple uncontrolled methods at launch.
Reporting manager first, then HR only where policy requires.
One primary calendar initially; add location-specific calendars only when genuinely required.
Staged invitations to pilot users, then remaining users after final readiness approval.
One designated email or collaboration channel with an issue template.

Kickoff with Sir Saud and nominated HR lead; confirm customer name, employee count, attendance approach and approval model; issue data templates; confirm pilot group; approve Phase 1 scope and timeline.

Configure tenant, branding, structure, roles, leave policies, holidays, schedules and dashboards in staging; import first data pack; deploy desktop agent to pilot devices; reconcile migration results.
Execute employee, leave, attendance, settings and dashboard UAT; fix critical/high defects; train DijiPeople/Maseer administrators and HR operations; freeze production configuration baseline.
Complete final data delta; run manager and employee training; complete production smoke tests; issue user guide; obtain UAT and go-live approvals; schedule user invitations and desktop rollout.
Enable production access; deploy attendance agent; validate first check-ins, leave request/approval and dashboard counts; open support channel and daily checkpoint.
Daily issue review, adoption tracking, configuration corrections, minor fixes and knowledge transfer to Maseer HR/IT champions.
Confirm acceptance, measure adoption, review lessons learned and prioritise recruitment/onboarding rollout.
Scope, owners and decision log opened.
No open critical defects; high defects have agreed treatment.
Sponsor, HR lead and DijiPeople sign-off.
First live attendance and leave transactions.
Stable operations and open items transferred to backlog/support.
Use live demonstrations in staging, role-based exercises and a short recorded recap. Do not put all users into one long generic session.
Objectives, scope, dashboard outcomes, responsibilities, decisions and go-live risks.
Tenant settings, structure, roles, users, employee data, leave policy and attendance configuration. Exercise: create/update a test employee and validate access.
Employee lifecycle, leave corrections, attendance exceptions, balance adjustment, reporting and audit trail. Exercise: resolve a sample exception end to end.
Team view, leave approval/rejection, attendance review, escalation and dashboard interpretation. Exercise: process a leave request.
Login, profile, leave request, balance, attendance, notifications and support. Exercise: submit and cancel a test leave request.
Installer deployment, update behaviour, device permissions, connectivity, troubleshooting and escalation.
Live Q&A, first transactions and issue capture.
Role-based quick-reference guide for employee, manager and HR administrator journeys.
Recorded or reusable demonstration covering the standard Phase 1 process.
Attendance desktop installation guide and troubleshooting checklist.
UAT scripts reused as hands-on training exercises.
Frequently asked questions and a support-escalation guide.
Training attendance and completion record for go-live evidence.
Can configure permitted settings, maintain an employee, correct an attendance exception and reconcile leave balances without DijiPeople intervention.
Can find their team, review attendance and complete a leave approval/rejection correctly.
Can sign in, view balance, submit leave and complete the agreed attendance action.
Can install/update the desktop agent and provide diagnostic information when escalating.
Create/import employee; update structure and manager; activate/deactivate; verify employee self-view and role restrictions.
Submit, approve, reject, cancel, attachment rule, insufficient balance, overlapping request and manager visibility.
Normal check-in/out, late arrival, missing event, weekend/holiday, shift assignment, correction and manager/HR review.
Branding, calendars, policy inheritance, permissions and effective-dated changes where applicable.
Headcount, leave and attendance counts reconcile to source transactions and respect role access.
Fresh install, update, offline/reconnect behaviour, antivirus response and no embedded production secret.
Cross-tenant isolation, unauthorised role access, suspended user and session expiry.
Outage, data loss/corruption, cross-tenant exposure, login failure for broad user groups or unusable attendance/leave process.
Must be fixed and retested before go-live.
Major process is blocked for a role or produces materially incorrect business results without a practical workaround.
Fix before go-live or obtain explicit sponsor risk acceptance with a dated fix.
Limited impact with a safe workaround; does not compromise data or core operation.
May enter post-go-live backlog with owner and target date.
Cosmetic, wording or minor convenience issue.
1. Freeze approved employee, leave-balance and attendance configuration files.
2. Create a production recovery point and verify monitoring and support contacts.
3. Apply production configuration and import final data/delta.
4. Run employee-count, hierarchy, leave-balance and shift reconciliations.
5. Smoke-test administrator, manager and employee accounts.
6. Send invitations in controlled batches, starting with HR, managers and pilot employees.
7. Deploy the desktop agent to approved devices and confirm the first attendance event.
8. Open the support channel, daily checkpoint and issue register.
System unavailable, data exposure, broad login or attendance outage
Immediate triage; protect data and restore service first.
Major function unavailable for a team or incorrect leave/attendance outcome
Workaround or fix prioritised in the next safe release.
Resolve through support, guidance or planned correction.
These are onboarding support targets, not a contractual SLA. A formal SLA should be agreed separately after the first-customer operating model is proven.
All approved active employees imported; duplicates resolved; manager, organisation, leave-balance and schedule reconciliation completed.
Pilot and production users can securely access the correct profile and permitted functions.
Standard request-to-approval cycle works and balances are accurate.
Agreed attendance method works on representative devices and exceptions can be corrected with an audit trail.
Maseer tenant, branding, structure, policies, calendars, roles and permissions are approved.
Published metrics reconcile to transactions and are visible only to authorised roles.
Required HR, manager, employee and IT sessions delivered; guides issued; champions identified.
Monitoring, backups, support channel, issue triage and rollback plan are operational.
No open critical defects; high defects are closed or explicitly accepted.
Recruitment: jobs, candidates, interviews, offers and hiring pipeline.
Phase 1 stable and HR process owners available.
Employee onboarding: documents, tasks, approvals, induction and conversion to employee.
Recruitment data model and handoff accepted.
Timesheets, payroll, performance, contracts and additional dashboards/integrations.
Business case, product readiness and support capacity confirmed.
Confirm whether the customer name is Maseer Group, Maseer Tech or another legal/display name.
Nominate the Maseer HR lead and IT representative.
Confirm attendance capture mode and pilot devices.
Approve leave types, policies, opening balances and approval route.
Approve pilot users and training attendee lists.

The rollout is feasible for the proposed scope and user count. The schedule is deliberately tight but realistic if Maseer provides complete data and accountable decision-makers in Week 1, and DijiPeople closes the production-readiness blockers before UAT.
